newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot propane stays steady in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot propane stays steady in quiet trade.

text.p: U.S. spot propane prices stayed steady in late trade on Friday, holding onto gains made on bullish inventory data released late Thursday, traders said.
In the U.S. Gulf Coast, Mont Belvieu spot propane remained between 50.75 cents and 51.00 cents a gallon, after gaining 1.25 cents this morning.
In the Midwest, spot propane traded at 50.00 cents, also unchanged from midday when a one cent gain was tallied, traders said.
Activity was light in late trade ahead of the weekend.
In its Thursday report, the Energy Information Administration said total U.S. stocks in propane fell 1.7 million barrels from Sept 30 to Oct 11 to 48.7 million.
The main trading hub of the U.S. Gulf Coast showed a 900,000 barrel draw and the Midwest showed an 800,000 drop.

Traders said the strong propane prices held up other liquids in the market, with normal butane in Belvieu ranging 53.00/53.25 cents. Normal butane was also helped up by short covering by petrochemical companies.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
